title: Group advantages, the GRPO loss, and the length bias
brief: Build group baselines and check them exactly, then the clipped GRPO loss with three ways to average over tokens. Watch GRPO's length bias appear on a toy, and run GRPO on Qwen3-0.6B with and without the Dr. GRPO fixes.
hints: Reshape rewards to (P, G) with rewards.view(-1, group_size), work along dim=1, and reshape back with .reshape(-1).
RLOO's baseline excludes the response itself. It equals G / (G - 1) * (r - group mean), which is one line.
grpo_advantages uses the population standard deviation: r.std(dim=1, unbiased=False). PyTorch's default is the Bessel-corrected one.
In clipped_surrogate, broadcast the advantages with advantages[:, None], and take torch.minimum of the unclipped and clipped products. The min is what makes the clip one-sided.

In aggregate, zero the padding with torch.where(mask > 0, per_token, 0) before summing, since padding can hold anything. sequence_mean divides each row by its own mask sum; token_mean divides everything by the total mask sum.

In length_bias_toy, build the batch fresh on every step from torch.log_softmax(logits, dim=1), and use torch.autograd.grad on your aggregate. Only column 1 of the token log-probs depends on the logits.
